title: Sharpness and uniqueness for positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s)
description:
Paper (49 pages) with its LaTeX sources and ancillary files (certificate scripts, data files and logs), and a Lean 4 formalisation of the paper's logical spine with its axiom ledger. Part II of a series; Part I is Positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s): near-criticality and uniqueness (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23197915). Preprint, October 2026; not yet peer-reviewed. Version 1.1 adds attributions and citations (the architecture of Viazovska’s construction, the Laplacian lemma of Alfes, Burban and Raum, Odlyzko’s Open Problem 2.2, and related work); the mathematics is unchanged. Version 1.2 credits Bondarenko, Radchenko and Seip as the precedent for removing all zeros of ζ and gives precise locators for the inputs from Part I; the mathematics is unchanged. Version 1.3 adds Corollary 8.2 and Appendix C: the Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if the classical Odlyzko–Poitou–Serre programme has no negative value, and for every prime-side gap up to log 2/(2π) the positive solutions are the same. It also reorganises the proof of positivity: Ξ2H is positive definite, which gives the sign of the normalising constant without computation, and the certified computations on which the positivity of H rests (a moment certificate for |t| ≤ 10.355 and the large-|t| bound from t = 9) use only the term c = 1 and the trivial bound for Kloosterman sums; the earlier window certificate is kept as an independent check.

Weil's explicit formula for ζ(s) equates a functional 𝒜(F), which depends only on the archimedean data of ζ, with sums over the zeros and over the prime powers. We construct an explicit even function F = Ξ2H, with H entire and positive on ℝ, such that F ≥ 0 and F̂ ≥ 0 on ℝ, F̂ vanishes at log n/(2π) for every integer n ≥ 2, and 𝒜(F) = 0. Since Ξ vanishes at every non-trivial zero, on or off the critical line, no information about the zeros is used. F is an exact magic function, as in the sphere-packing bounds of Cohn–Elkies and Viazovska, for the linear programme of Odlyzko, Poitou and Serre: for the data of ζ the programme has optimal value at most 0, so the method is sharp, and under RH F is a minimiser. With a support theorem of Part I, every positive solution of the formula, with prime measure beyond log 2/(2π), is then ζ's own. This resolves Conjectures S and U of Part I. Moreover, RH holds if and only if this classical programme has optimal value exactly 0. H comes from an eigenvalue-¼ eigenfunction of the hyperbolic Laplacian through a contour argument of Viazovska's type, with Green's identity in place of Cauchy's theorem; its positivity is partly computer-assisted. We do not prove RH; by these results it is equivalent to the existence of such a positive solution.

The Lean 4 formalisation (paper/anc/lean) builds on that of Part I, version 1.3 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23217537). It states the main results (Theorems 1 and 2 and Corollaries 3 and 8.2, the latter except the zero set in its part (a) and its clause (c)(iv)) in Lean, with every difference from the paper's statements listed in FAITHFUL.md, and proves them from Mathlib, six axioms of Part I's ledger and an explicit axiom ledger of two axioms of its own (an analytic lemma proved in the paper, and the existence of the object constructed in the paper with its properties; the construction itself is not formalised); it contains no sorry, and its build and audit run in continuous integration.

This paper was produced by AI agents, mainly Anthropic's Claude with supplementary assistance from OpenAI's Astra, under the author's direction; it has not yet been checked by a human expert.
